statement.document_title: Three ideas from linguistics that everyone in AI should know

from_speaker: lack ties to dynamically updated cognitive models
refer to an external world, or an update-able cognitive model thereof
our_interpretation: Reference means reference to the external world, as the surrounding text explicitly states. Tracking an entity mentioned in a passage is not sufficient by itself.

The ordinary reading of dynamically updated cognitive models is internal representations of the world that can change as relevant information changes. No particular architecture or benchmark is imposed.
Such systems refers to the contemporary neural language systems discussed in the footnote, including GPT-3. It is not expanded to every neural system or to later models.
Because this describes an ongoing technical state without a reporting cycle, the target is a snapshot of systems current on the post date, 2022-06-22.
Pretty is treated as rhetorical description, not a separately measurable proposition.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence about the intended contemporary systems establishes both that their states lack external-world reference and that they lack ties to dynamically updated representations of that world. Failure on selected prompts or absence of a named architectural module alone is insufficient.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes external-world reference or ties to dynamically updated cognitive models in an in-scope system as it existed at the post date. Discourse tracking, semantic similarity, or task-specific state changes alone are insufficient.
